1.support: We aimed to compare PEEP titration strategies based on electrical impedance tomography (EIT) to methods derived from respiratory system mechanics with or without esophageal pressure measurements

2.support: Nineteen adult patients, admitted to the Medical ICU of the University Hospital of Angers, France, from December 2019 to April 2020 were enrolled within 24 h after the diagnosis of ARDS defined according to the Berlin criteria.

3.support: According to the Berlin definition, severe, moderate, and mild ARDS were present at enrollment in 6 (32%), 10 (53%) and 3 (16%) patients, respectively.
3.location: Page 3, Results, Patients' characteristics; Table 1, Page 4

4.support: The report describes eligibility criteria but does not state whether all eligible patients screened during the period were enrolled or report screening counts.

5.support: the number of included patients is relatively small

6.support: PEEP level was increased at 20 cmH2O then was progressively decreased by steps of 3 cmH2O every 3 min, until PEEP reached 5 cmH2O.
6.location: Page 3, Methods, Decremental PEEP trial; Pages 2-3, Patients' installation and settings

7.support: In a sample of 9 patients from the present cohort, ΔEELVEIT correlated well with ΔEELV measured by the single breath method (rho 0.716, p = 0.037

8.support: The report does not describe any blinding or masking of the investigators assessing the physiological outcomes.

9.support: Esophageal pressure data were missing for one patient, due to a technical limitation.

10.support: Statistical comparisons were performed using a Mann–Whitney U-test for simple comparisons. For multiples comparisons, Friedman test or ANOVA were performed as appropriate
10.location: Page 3, Methods, Statistical analysis; e.g. Table 2 ANOVA p values, Page 7

11.support: The primary pre-to-post outcomes (R/Iest, ΔPaO2/FiO2, ΔCRS) were computed from single paired measurements at PEEP 15 and 5 cmH2O, not from a repeated-measures interrupted time-series design.
11.location: Page 3, Methods, Evaluation of response to PEEP in terms of oxygenation and compliance

12.support: The intervention (PEEP titration with esophageal and EIT monitoring) was applied at the individual patient level, not at a group level.

nih.rationale: Fair: the study question, eligibility criteria, intervention and physiological outcome measures are clearly described and objectively measured (items 1, 2, 6, 7), follow-up was essentially complete (item 9) and formal statistical testing with p values was performed (item 10). It falls short of Good because the sample was small with no power justification (item 5), it was not reported whether all eligible patients were enrolled (item 4), outcome assessors were not blinded (item 8), and the design lacked multiple pre/post measurement periods (item 11), all of which limit confidence in attributing the observed physiological changes to the PEEP-titration intervention.
